gaps.sentence: All candidates must ___ the written exam in June.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'exam' from the candidate's side
gaps.explanation: take an exam (or sit an exam) means to be tested; 'give an exam' is not used in British English.

gaps.sentence: Grandad's best man ___ a joke that made everyone laugh.
gaps.explanation: tell a joke is the fixed collocation; 'say a joke' is not used.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ a diary since she was twelve.
gaps.explanation: keep a diary is the fixed collocation for writing in one regularly.

gaps.sentence: Her company ___ a huge profit last year.
gaps.explanation: make a profit (or make a loss) is the fixed business collocation.

gaps.sentence: We were asked to ___ an experiment in the laboratory.
gaps.explanation: do an experiment is the standard collocation in scientific contexts.

gaps.sentence: Stop ___ money on things you never use.
gaps.hint: to use money on useless things; -ing form after 'Stop'
gaps.explanation: waste money on something means to spend it on useless things; 'stop' is followed by the -ing form.

gaps.sentence: He always ___ the truth, however unpleasant it is.
gaps.explanation: tell the truth is the fixed collocation; 'say the truth' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: I'd rather ___ by card than carry cash.
gaps.explanation: pay by card/in cash is the fixed pattern for the method of payment.
